text:
mike: Heads up — seeing node_exporter heartbeats missing on ~6 GPU nodes in us-west2. Prom scrape shows ~2m lag, DCGM metrics stalled. conntrack count is near system max on those nodes. Anybody touching kube-proxy/CNI?
jana: noticed spikes in model loads earlier, maybe TCP connections not closing. do we have conntrack metrics per-pod? :thinking_face:
alex: ran `conntrack -C` on node-12 — ~200k entries (limit 262144). kube-proxy logs show repeated NAT table updates after the calico MTU bump last night.
mike: calico MTU bump rolled at 03:15 UTC yesterday. also saw an OOM kill on the runtime-metrics sidecar on node-12; exporter restarted and I think the restart created a connection storm to model endpoints.
sre-bot: Alert fired: exporter_heartbeat_missing (us-west2-gpu-pool) — group: eng-infra — severity: high
ops: quick triage options: bump conntrack max or reduce ephemeral sockets. temporary: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=400000` but this needs infra approval and a persistent node config.
jana: temporary bump makes sense for immediate relief. longer term we should add backpressure in the agent: limit concurrent upstream connections in the GPU agent (runtime-metrics sidecar), and enable HTTP keepalives so restarts don't create connection storms.
alex: also can tune Prometheus scrapes — we currently have `scrape_interval: 15s` and `scrape_timeout: 10s` for DCGM targets. With frequent exporter restarts that generates a backlog. For the DCGM job maybe increase timeout to 30s or add `honor_timestamps: false` to reduce cardinality churn.
mike: careful about increasing timeouts — hides failures. prefer alert suppression: only page after 5m of missing heartbeats and add an exclusion for nodes labelled `rolling-upgrade=true`.
ops: proposed plan: (1) patch agent to cap concurrent outbound sockets, (2) deploy a cluster-wide conntrack_max bump via a NodePool init script, (3) ship a DaemonSet init to set nf_conntrack_max on boot for older nodes, (4) add Prometheus relabeling to drop noisy ephemeral connection metrics from exporter.
mike: rolling update approach: cordon + drain one node in canary set, restart exporter sidecar, watch `conntrack -L | wc -l`. If stable for 10m, continue. also measure GPU utilization — idle GPUs in that pool are costing approx $1500/day right now.
jana: I'll draft the k8s job and run on a 2-node canary subset first. will also propose SLO tweak: make gpu_exporter_heartbeat a 10m window for pager to reduce noisy pages during rolling work.
alex: opening PR for agent connection cap (`agent/connlimit#34`). tagging @infra-oncall for approval.
infra-oncall: acknowledged. schedule a maintenance window at 11:30 UTC to run canary. will monitor Grafana dashboard `GPU Fleet / Exporters` and paging rules.
mike: quick triage commands for anyone on shift:
```
# check conntrack count
sudo conntrack -C
# force restart exporter daemonset
kubectl -n gpu-system rollout restart ds/gpu-exporter
# tail exporter logs
kubectl -n gpu-system logs $(kubectl -n gpu-system get pods -l app=gpu-exporter -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -c exporter | tail -n 200
```
ops: if canary looks good we'll bake the sysctl into the node image and roll the rest via normal pool upgrade. also adding a liveness probe to exporter to avoid silent OOM cycles is a good idea.
mike: summary of PRs/refs: infra/conntrack-sysctl#12, agent/connlimit#34, monitoring/prom-scrape#78. I'll update this thread with canary results. :white_check_mark:
